claims.text: The proposed method incorporates machine-learning potentials into ab initio molecular dynamics.
Incorporating machine-learning potentials into ab initio molecular dynamics will substantially reduce the cost of computing fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed approach is intended for multicomponent high-entropy systems at high temperature.
The approach covers both solid and fluid states of high-entropy systems.
The proposed approach will retain the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy contributions.
Machine-learning potentials improve computational efficiency relative to explicit ab initio workflows.

Potential-based molecular dynamics can reproduce selected structural, stability, ordering, and mechanical properties of a multicomponent Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni high-entropy alloy in quantitative agreement with first-principles calculations and experiments.
The proposed method will reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties relative to explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation and TOR-TILD.
The proposed method will improve accuracy relative to explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation and TOR-TILD.
The accuracy of the machine-learning potentials limits the proposed method.
Computational resources and the complexity of high-entropy systems limit the proposed method.
A comparison against explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation and TOR-TILD can test the proposed method using computational cost and thermodynamic-property accuracy.
